claims.notes: p-adic valuation: 1/p^k is the unique term of valuation -k.

claims.summary: Open Erdős 828 at a = 0: infinitely many n with φ(n) | n.
claims.notes: Statement is type_of% (Erdos828.erdos_828 0). Powers of two. Well known and easy; says nothing about general a.

claims.summary: Open Erdős 828 at a = -1: infinitely many n with φ(n) | n - 1.
claims.notes: Statement is type_of% (Erdos828.erdos_828 (-1)). All primes. Well known and easy.

claims.summary: f(2) = 7: the smallest tournament in which every pair of vertices is dominated by a third has 7 vertices.
claims.notes: Every in-neighbourhood carries an S_1 sub-tournament, so in-degrees are ≥ 3 and 3m ≤ m(m-1)/2. Upper bound from upstream f_two_le (complete proof).

Because f is an sInf over ℕ (0 if no tournament has property S_n), the formal statement also asserts that S_n tournaments exist for every n; the proof covers both: the in-neighbourhood recursion f(n) ≥ 2f(n−1)+1 and Erdős's probabilistic existence argument as a counting/union bound. Not a misformalization (both parts are true and due to Erdős), but the statement is stronger than the informal lower bound alone.

claims.summary: 1 is not a congruent number (Fermat's right-triangle theorem).
claims.notes: Clears denominators to C^4 - (2L)^4 = (A^2 - B^2)^2 and proves x^4 - y^4 = z^2 has no solutions with y, z ≠ 0 by Fermat descent (own proof; Mathlib only has the sum form not_fermat_42). Signed sides are allowed by the definition; the proof does not need positivity.

claims.summary: n(2) = 6 (Erdős–Rubin–Taylor): the smallest bipartite graph that is not 2-choosable has 6 vertices.
claims.notes: K_{3,3} with lists {1,2},{1,3},{2,3}; every 2-colourable graph on ≤ 5 vertices is 2-choosable (side-colouring + pigeonhole); Hall's theorem for card-choosability.
